title: Estimating causal effects of treatments in randomized and nonrandomized studies
authors: Donald B. Rubin
access_depth: Abstract and bibliographic metadata inspected; no full-text claim
contribution: Clarifies how experimental assignment and carefully controlled observational comparisons support treatment-effect estimation.
key_findings: Randomization is preferred when feasible; observational adjustment requires explicit conditions rather than treating association as intervention.
importance: Supplies the causal vocabulary needed to turn a checker audit into a verdict-intervention experiment.
relevance: Historical R/U trajectories differ beyond their terminal verdict; exact-source equality alone does not make them randomized counterfactuals.
transferable_idea: Freeze candidate and history, randomize the delivered verdict at onset, and define potential outcomes separately for unsafe acceptance and legitimate-request denial.
limitations: Theory does not retrospectively repair missing receipts or justify generalization from five chosen families.

title: Statistics and Causal Inference
authors: Paul W. Holland
venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association 81(396):945–960
access_depth: Primary full-text introduction and potential-outcome sections inspected
contribution: Formalizes causal effects through potential outcomes and distinguishes causal questions from associational descriptions.
key_findings: Individual counterfactual contrasts require assumptions; randomized assignment supports population-average contrasts under a defined design.
importance: Separates three issues often conflated in the draft: identification, statistical precision, and population transport.
relevance: A selected secure onset can support a controlled within-onset comparison even though it represents no broad task population.
transferable_idea: State which state is cloned, which random inputs are coupled, and whether the target is a finite scheduled-cohort effect or a superpopulation effect.
limitations: Cloning software does not eliminate model-runtime drift, interference, or the need to define the unit.

title: The central role of the propensity score in observational studies for causal effects
authors: Paul R. Rosenbaum; Donald B. Rubin
access_depth: Abstract and bibliographic metadata inspected; no full-text claim
contribution: Shows how treatment-assignment probabilities can summarize observed covariates for observational adjustment.
key_findings: Balancing the propensity score can remove observed-covariate imbalance under the paper's assumptions; it cannot remove unmeasured confounding.
importance: Provides a precise boundary on what matching can accomplish.
relevance: The manuscript's same-source matches are useful forensic evidence, but task history, schedule position, and latent runtime conditions remain unmatched.
transferable_idea: Use this as a negative design lesson: prefer randomized verdict forks to elaborate propensity adjustment of tiny historical cohorts.
limitations: Five families and sparse treatment histories cannot support credible high-dimensional propensity estimation; source matching is not a substitute for exchangeability.

title: Principal Stratification in Causal Inference
authors: Constantine E. Frangakis; Donald B. Rubin
access_depth: Abstract and bibliographic metadata inspected; no full-text claim
contribution: Defines treatment-effect estimands using strata determined by joint potential values of an intermediate variable.
key_findings: Ordinary adjustment for post-treatment variables can lack causal interpretation; principal strata are unaffected by realized assignment.
importance: Illuminates selection when eligibility itself depends on a method or policy.
relevance: Secure onset precedes verdict randomization, so it is legitimate eligibility for that contrast; it becomes post-treatment when comparing precursor models or repair policies.
transferable_idea: Report onset probability and the conditional preservation effect separately. Compare models on common seeded candidates or define a principal-stratum target with explicit identification limits.
limitations: Principal strata are generally not directly observable; invoking the framework does not identify them automatically.

title: A structural approach to selection bias
authors: Miguel A. Hernán; Sonia Hernández-Díaz; James M. Robins
access_depth: Abstract and bibliographic metadata inspected; no full-text claim
contribution: Uses causal diagrams to unify selection biases that arise from conditioning on common effects.
key_findings: Selection and confounding have different causal structures and therefore require different remedies.
importance: Makes the study's eligibility, timeout, and completion mechanisms scientifically visible.
relevance: Models that reach secure onsets on different families can appear differently robust simply because their eligible populations differ.
transferable_idea: Draw separate diagrams for precursor success, verdict assignment, technical completion, and terminal outcomes; retain all prescheduled failures and no-onset cases.
limitations: Not every restriction is collider bias. Conditioning on onset before randomized verdict assignment narrows the target without necessarily biasing that randomized contrast.

title: Pseudoreplication and the Design of Ecological Field Experiments
authors: Stuart H. Hurlbert
access_depth: Abstract and bibliographic metadata inspected; no full-text claim
contribution: Analyzes experimental designs that mistake repeated samples for independent treatment replication.
key_findings: Non-independent observations and unreplicated treatments can produce inappropriate error terms; spatial or temporal interspersion matters.
importance: An influential warning against increasing apparent evidence by multiplying observations inside a few experimental units.
relevance: Repeated CSRF seeds, repeated candidate hashes, and many tool calls do not create new security mechanisms or independent task families.
transferable_idea: Allocate budget to diverse reviewed families before multiplying seeds; randomize and interleave treatment arms across collection time.
limitations: Ecological recommendations must be translated to software dependence structures, not copied as a universal requirement for one specific statistical test.

title: The Language-as-Fixed-Effect Fallacy: A Critique of Language Statistics in Psychological Research
authors: Herbert H. Clark
venue: Journal of Verbal Learning and Verbal Behavior 12(4):335–359
access_depth: Indexed primary-paper abstract and opening section inspected
contribution: Shows why conclusions about language cannot ignore variation across the particular stimuli chosen for an experiment.
key_findings: Treating sampled materials as fixed can support stronger generalization than the data warrant.
importance: Offers a close analogy for benchmark studies that generalize from a small convenience set of tasks.
relevance: Twenty authored families can still share templates, mechanisms, and answer spaces; a family label alone does not prove independence.
transferable_idea: Define a task sampling frame, document shared generators, and test transfer to withheld mechanisms and independently authored tasks.
limitations: The paper is about psychological materials; the relevant transfer is its sampling logic, not its original analysis formula.

title: Random effects structure for confirmatory hypothesis testing: Keep it maximal
authors: Dale J. Barr; Roger Levy; Christoph Scheepers; Harry J. Tily
access_depth: Primary author-manuscript metadata and indexed methods/discussion excerpts inspected
contribution: Investigates how random-effects structure affects confirmatory inference with crossed experimental units.
key_findings: Simulations show that omitting relevant random slopes can compromise generalization and Type I error control.
importance: Explains why a task intercept alone need not represent heterogeneous treatment responses.
relevance: The verdict effect may vary by family, model, and initial candidate; pooling submissions ignores that structure.
transferable_idea: Prespecify task-level treatment contrasts and a hierarchy that reflects the actual randomization; simulate analysis behavior before choosing a large mixed model.
limitations: Maximal fitting is not automatically appropriate for a small binary dataset; read with Matuschek et al. and use a convergence fallback.

title: The Hitchhiker’s Guide to Testing Statistical Significance in Natural Language Processing
authors: Rotem Dror; Gili Baumer; Segev Shlomov; Roi Reichart
access_depth: Abstract and bibliographic metadata inspected; no full-text claim
contribution: Provides an experimental-setup-aware guide to significance testing in NLP.
key_findings: Test choice depends on the evaluation measure, pairing, distributional assumptions, and intended comparison.
importance: Useful practical bridge between statistical theory and model-evaluation practice.
relevance: The draft has paired branches, nested seeds, multiple endpoints, and technical missingness; one generic test cannot address every analysis.
transferable_idea: Prespecify a primary directional outcome, family-level paired estimates, uncertainty procedure, and multiplicity policy before collecting confirmatory data.
limitations: This methodological paper does not validate the security oracle and does not justify testing a collection of selectively reported pilot outcomes.

title: Statistical Comparisons of Classifiers over Multiple Data Sets
authors: Janez Demšar
access_depth: Abstract and bibliographic metadata inspected; no full-text claim
contribution: Studies comparisons between learning algorithms across multiple datasets.
key_findings: Recommends paired nonparametric comparisons and multi-method procedures under the examined conditions.
importance: Shifts attention from repeated observations on one dataset to consistent behavior across datasets.
relevance: Task-family paired effects are more informative here than treating all 45 repeated submissions as independent evidence.
transferable_idea: Show the distribution of family-specific preservation and harm contrasts, not just one pooled percentage.
limitations: Ranks can discard effect-size information, and standard dataset-level tests still need a justified independent sampling unit; five selected families provide very limited resolution.

title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
authors: Gavin C. Cawley; Nicola L. C. Talbot
access_depth: Abstract and bibliographic metadata inspected; no full-text claim
contribution: Shows that optimization of a noisy evaluation criterion can overfit model selection itself.
key_findings: Selection-induced performance distortion can be comparable to apparent differences between algorithms.
importance: Explains why repeated methodological refinement against observed pilots can create a convincing but unstable story.
relevance: The repository contains sequential waves and evolving endpoints after inspection of earlier outcomes.
transferable_idea: Use old cohorts for hypothesis formation; freeze interventions and outcomes on development families, then evaluate once on untouched families.
limitations: The result concerns model-selection procedures; applying it here is an analogy to adaptive research decisions, not proof that a particular pilot effect is spurious.

title: The reusable holdout: Preserving validity in adaptive data analysis
authors: Cynthia Dwork; Vitaly Feldman; Moritz Hardt; Toniann Pitassi; Omer Reingold; Aaron Roth
access_depth: Abstract and bibliographic metadata inspected; no full-text claim
contribution: Develops a way to preserve validation under adaptively chosen analyses using ideas from differential privacy.
key_findings: Repeated access to evaluation data can invalidate ordinary fixed-analysis reasoning; carefully controlled access can limit that problem.
importance: Provides a theoretical basis for separating exploration from confirmation.
relevance: The many source-bound recounts are valuable audits but do not turn the same outcomes into fresh confirmatory evidence.
transferable_idea: Create a genuinely untouched validation partition and keep a ledger of which decisions used development results; sophisticated reusable-holdout machinery is optional.
limitations: The method's assumptions and privacy-style accounting would need implementation; merely naming a holdout or preregistration does not provide its guarantee.

title: Time-uniform, nonparametric, nonasymptotic confidence sequences
authors: Steven R. Howard; Aaditya Ramdas; Jon McAuliffe; Jasjeet Sekhon
access_depth: Abstract and bibliographic metadata inspected; no full-text claim
contribution: Constructs confidence intervals that remain valid uniformly over observation time under stated stochastic conditions.
key_findings: Supports sequential estimation without pretending that the stopping sample size was fixed in advance.
importance: Relevant when expensive model experiments need principled monitoring or early termination.
relevance: The pilot waves stopped technically and were followed by new waves; future adaptive collection needs explicit inferential treatment.
transferable_idea: Consider an anytime-valid design over independent family blocks if scientific stopping will depend on accumulating results; retain a separate plan for technical interruptions.
limitations: Confidence sequences do not fix informative missingness, dependent family sampling, or post hoc endpoint changes; ordinary clustered estimators cannot simply be relabeled anytime-valid.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning at the Edge of the Statistical Precipice
authors: Rishabh Agarwal; Max Schwarzer; Pablo Samuel Castro; Aaron C. Courville; Marc G. Bellemare
access_depth: Abstract and bibliographic metadata inspected; no full-text claim
contribution: Examines unreliable conclusions from few-run evaluations on multi-task reinforcement-learning benchmarks.
key_findings: Interval estimates, performance profiles, and robust aggregates can reveal uncertainty hidden by point estimates.
importance: Offers an unusually close evaluation analogue for costly agent runs with nested task and seed variation.
relevance: The manuscript's single-seed historical cells cannot resolve within-cell variability, while repeated CSRF seeds cannot replace broader task coverage.
transferable_idea: Use paired family summaries and transparent outcome profiles, including missing scheduled slots; simulate precision across both tasks and seeds.
limitations: RL aggregate recommendations do not automatically transfer to rare binary security failures; avoid reporting an interquartile mean that hides severe tail harms.

title: Construct Validity in Psychological Tests
authors: Lee J. Cronbach; Paul E. Meehl
access_depth: Primary-paper opening conceptual sections inspected
contribution: Distinguishes evidence for a theoretical construct from superficial agreement with an observed test score.
key_findings: Validation requires a network of justified relationships between the construct and its operational measures.
importance: Provides the conceptual foundation missing when action count is described as persistence or API change as strategy change.
relevance: The runner's self-termination label mostly measures reminder exhaustion, while finite-test PASS measures only authored examples.
transferable_idea: Define each intended construct, its observable indicators, alternative explanations, and disconfirming tests in a compact measurement table.
limitations: Psychometric constructs and executable security properties differ; use the validation logic without implying that all security judgments require latent-variable modeling.

title: Convergent and discriminant validation by the multitrait-multimethod matrix
authors: Donald T. Campbell; Donald W. Fiske
access_depth: Primary-paper opening section and bibliographic record inspected
contribution: Separates agreement across methods measuring one construct from apparent agreement caused by shared measurement methods.
key_findings: Construct validation needs both convergence and discrimination; repeated use of one method can create misleading consistency.
importance: Explains why two independently coded checkers may still share one erroneous specification.
relevance: The raw checker, bounded reference, and policy gate assess different things and sometimes share authored assumptions.
transferable_idea: Audit a matrix of properties by methods: exploit tests, legitimate-use tests, finite proofs, and independent expert adjudication. Investigate disagreement instead of majority-voting it away.
limitations: Correlations alone cannot establish security or independence; the proposed matrix is a validation framework, not a replacement oracle.

title: Measurement and Fairness
authors: Abigail Z. Jacobs; Hanna Wallach
access_depth: Abstract and bibliographic metadata inspected; no full-text claim
contribution: Transfers measurement modeling from social science to computational fairness.
key_findings: Harms can arise from mismatches between a construct and the measurable proxy used to operationalize it.
importance: Offers a modern computational formulation of the manuscript's central audit problem.
relevance: Unavailability was operationalized as a hidden veto, and stopping as an adapter event; both mismatches alter the scientific meaning of observed behavior.
transferable_idea: Write a validity argument for each label and preserve separate property, policy, communication, and controller layers in the data model.
limitations: Fairness is the paper's application domain; using its framework here is a proposed methodological transfer rather than evidence about coding agents.

title: AI and the Everything in the Whole Wide World Benchmark
authors: Inioluwa Deborah Raji; Emily M. Bender; Amandalynne Paullada; Emily Denton; Alex Hanna
access_depth: Abstract and bibliographic metadata inspected; no full-text claim
contribution: Critiques treating influential benchmarks as general measures of progress toward broad AI capabilities.
key_findings: Benchmark framing can exceed the construct validity supplied by particular tasks and scoring rules.
importance: An important prior argument against universal capability claims from narrow evaluation suites.
relevance: The current finite-language tasks can establish bounded contradictions, not general inability to repair software or understand impossibility.
transferable_idea: State the task universe and claim boundary in the title, abstract, and benchmark documentation; evaluate transfer rather than assuming it.
limitations: This is a peer-reviewed position paper, not a prevalence study of oracle defects or an empirical estimate of agent behavior.

title: The Benchmark Lottery
authors: Mostafa Dehghani; Yi Tay; Alexey A. Gritsenko; Zhe Zhao; Neil Houlsby; Fernando Diaz; Donald Metzler; Oriol Vinyals
access_depth: arXiv abstract/metadata and indexed submitted-manuscript header inspected
contribution: Investigates how benchmark composition affects apparent algorithm superiority.
key_findings: Changing the selected tasks can substantially change relative rankings across several ML domains.
importance: Challenges the assumption that one aggregate captures an intrinsic method quality.
relevance: The guidance contrast is driven by two historical families, and later false-feedback results concentrate in CSRF.
transferable_idea: Publish family-level contrasts, predeclared family weights, leave-family-out sensitivity, and transfer to separately authored mechanisms.
limitations: The inspected primary sources establish a preprint and NeurIPS submission, not a verified accepted venue; its examples do not establish how large lottery effects are in this study.

title: Leakage and the reproducibility crisis in machine-learning-based science
authors: Sayash Kapoor; Arvind Narayanan
access_depth: Primary full-text summary, taxonomy, and discussion excerpts inspected
contribution: Develops a taxonomy of leakage and connects performance evaluation to the scientific claims it is used to support.
key_findings: A reproducibility case study removes claimed superiority of complex models after methodological errors are corrected.
importance: Distinguishes reproducible computation from a valid scientific inference.
relevance: The repository's strong hashes and replay tests establish consistency but cannot establish that the checker measured security or that guidance lacked answer cues.
transferable_idea: Add a compact claim-to-evidence argument and hold out task templates, retrieval examples, and validation mutations by mechanism.
limitations: Leakage is only one validity threat here; missing receipts and a hidden veto should not be mislabeled as training-data leakage.

title: Statistical Comparisons of Classifiers by Generalized Stochastic Dominance
authors: Christoph Jansen; Malte Nalenz; Georg Schollmeyer; Thomas Augustin
access_depth: Abstract and bibliographic metadata inspected; no full-text claim
contribution: Provides a comparison framework for algorithms across multiple datasets and multiple quality criteria using preference systems.
key_findings: Generalized stochastic dominance can compare performance without committing to a single potentially inconsistent aggregate.
importance: Directly relevant when security, functionality, and verification cost cannot be collapsed without value judgments.
relevance: The same binary regression outcome currently combines denying legitimate requests with accepting retired keys.
transferable_idea: Display the unsafe-acceptance, false-denial, and resource-cost vector; report Pareto-dominated policies before considering weighted utility.
limitations: The full dominance procedure needs sufficient data and justified preferences; a small pilot should use descriptive frontiers rather than claim a statistically established ordering.

title: Rational use of cognitive resources in human planning
authors: Frederick Callaway; Bas van Opheusden; Sayan Gul; Priyam Das; Paul M. Krueger; Thomas L. Griffiths; Falk Lieder
access_depth: Abstract and bibliographic metadata inspected; no full-text claim
contribution: Models planning as resource-constrained allocation of computation and tests the predictions with human behavior.
key_findings: People adapt planning strategies to circumstances; a single heuristic does not explain every condition.
importance: Motivates evaluating adaptive decision policies against explicit costs instead of equating fewer steps with better reasoning.
relevance: The current study treats stopping counts descriptively, without a payoff model determining when inspection or revision is worthwhile.
transferable_idea: Vary checker reliability, audit cost, and repairability, then compare observed edit/audit/stop choices against a bounded optimal reference.
limitations: Human evidence is not evidence of the same mechanism in LLMs. The publisher correction changes author order, reflected here.

title: Safe Reinforcement Learning via Shielding under Partial Observability
authors: Steven Carr; Nils Jansen; Sebastian Junges; Ufuk Topcu
access_depth: Abstract and bibliographic metadata inspected; no full-text claim
contribution: Integrates safety shields with reinforcement learning when the agent has incomplete observations.
key_findings: Carefully integrated shields can preserve safety and improve learning performance; some settings permit removing an initially conservative shield.
importance: Provides a precedent for studying the performance cost of conservative safety enforcement.
relevance: The CSRF reject-all behavior preserves one prohibition while destroying legitimate functionality, so safety constraints and useful behavior must be evaluated together.
transferable_idea: Compare advice-only checking with a bounded property-preserving intervention, and measure overblocking and recovery alongside violations.
limitations: Shield guarantees depend on the model and specification supplied; an incorrect shield could reproduce the manuscript's evaluator defect.

title: The Optimal Control of Partially Observable Markov Processes over a Finite Horizon
authors: Richard D. Smallwood; Edward J. Sondik
access_depth: Abstract and bibliographic metadata inspected; no full-text claim
contribution: Formulates finite-horizon control when internal states are hidden and observations are probabilistic.
key_findings: Shows a piecewise-linear, convex optimal payoff over belief states and outlines a policy-computation algorithm.
importance: Supplies an exact reference model for small, controlled checker-reliability experiments.
relevance: The agent may be uncertain whether code is defective, feedback is wrong, or an input is unavailable; its next action should depend on that belief.
transferable_idea: Construct a deliberately small latent-state benchmark whose edit, audit, and stop policy can be solved exactly and compared with agent decisions.
limitations: An exact POMDP abstraction is only as valid as its assumed transitions, observation likelihoods, and losses; real repository repair is vastly larger.

title: Planning and acting in partially observable stochastic domains
authors: Leslie Pack Kaelbling; Michael L. Littman; Anthony R. Cassandra
access_depth: Publisher abstract and primary technical-report introduction inspected
contribution: Develops planning methods that maintain uncertainty about state and choose actions under partial observability.
key_findings: Actions can have informational value as well as directly advancing the objective; finite-memory policies are possible in some cases.
importance: Reframes inspection as a potentially rational information-gathering action.
relevance: The older false-FAIL arms inspect more but submit fewer candidates; counting only edits could misdescribe their response.
transferable_idea: Separate information actions from code-changing actions and measure whether each audit changes subsequent decisions or only consumes budget.
limitations: The existence of an information-gathering interpretation does not show that these agents maintain calibrated beliefs or act optimally.

title: Principles of metareasoning
authors: Stuart Russell; Eric Wefald
access_depth: Abstract and bibliographic metadata inspected; no full-text claim
contribution: Treats computational operations as decisions whose value derives from their effect on subsequent external actions.
key_findings: Probability and utility can justify when additional reasoning is worth its resource cost.
importance: Establishes that cost-aware stopping and value-of-computation are longstanding ideas, not new contributions available merely by renaming them.
relevance: The paper's opportunity is to instantiate and test these principles for uncertain repair feedback.
transferable_idea: Measure the benefit of an audit through changed preserve/edit/escalate decisions, and compare against no-audit, always-audit, and bounded-optimal policies.
limitations: The theoretical framework does not supply empirical transition probabilities or a calibrated security loss for the proposed benchmark.

title: Selecting Computations: Theory and Applications
authors: Nicholas Hay; Stuart Russell; David Tolpin; Solomon Eyal Shimony
access_depth: Abstract and bibliographic metadata inspected; no full-text claim
contribution: Develops metalevel decision theory for selecting computations in Bayesian selection problems.
key_findings: Derives sampling results and demonstrates that bandit heuristics can be inappropriate for one-shot decisions.
importance: Clarifies that choosing information before one consequential decision differs from repeatedly earning rewards.
relevance: An independent audit is valuable if it changes which repair decision is selected, not because it increases an abstract confidence score.
transferable_idea: Use a finite stopping baseline that prices audits and explicitly includes preserving the current program, editing it, and escalating uncertainty.
limitations: The framework's optimality claims depend on its decision model; do not transfer its bounds unchanged to correlated checker outputs.

title: Rational Use of Cognitive Resources: Levels of Analysis Between the Computational and the Algorithmic
authors: Thomas L. Griffiths; Falk Lieder; Noah D. Goodman
access_depth: Publisher abstract and selected full-text resource-rationality sections inspected
contribution: Introduces resource-rational analysis as a bridge between abstract goals and implementable cognitive algorithms.
key_findings: Apparent departures from unconstrained optimality may follow from rational allocation of limited computational resources.
importance: Warns against calling continued repair irrational without specifying available evidence and action costs.
relevance: The hidden veto supplies misleading evidence; the observer's knowledge of that veto is not the agent's knowledge.
transferable_idea: Define an information-matched reference policy and vary the cost of checking, editing, and stopping before interpreting agent behavior.
limitations: Human cognitive models are an analogy here; the proposal must be falsifiable rather than a post hoc story that rationalizes every action.

title: Balancing Type I error and power in linear mixed models
authors: Hannes Matuschek; Reinhold Kliegl; Shravan Vasishth; Harald Baayen; Douglas Bates
access_depth: Abstract and bibliographic metadata inspected; no full-text claim
contribution: Examines the power costs of overly complex random-effects structures.
key_findings: Simulations show that unsupported maximal structures can lose power and that suitable model selection can balance error control and power.
importance: Provides a useful counterpoint to mechanically adopting the most elaborate hierarchical model.
relevance: The proposed study has many conditions but likely few independent families and sparse directional security events.
transferable_idea: Simulate the planned estimator on plausible family heterogeneity and missingness, and prespecify an interpretable fallback if the hierarchical fit fails.
limitations: These simulations concern linear mixed models; binary paired outcomes require their own design-specific checks rather than borrowed numerical guarantees.

title: On optimum recognition error and reject tradeoff
authors: C. K. Chow
access_depth: Publisher abstract and bibliographic metadata plus primary MIT report abstract inspected; no full-text claim
contribution: Analyzes an optimal rejection rule and the relation between classification errors and rejected predictions.
key_findings: Abstention trades coverage against errors instead of automatically constituting a desirable outcome.
importance: Foundational precedent for measuring refusal as a cost-bearing decision.
relevance: The CSRF reject-all endpoint cannot be called a successful safety response merely because it accepts no unauthorized request.
transferable_idea: Report useful coverage together with false acceptance and false denial, and compare policies under explicit asymmetric error costs.
limitations: Static recognition decisions lack the action-dependent program state and evolving evidence of sequential code repair; optimal rejection guarantees cannot be transferred directly.

title: On the Foundations of Noise-free Selective Classification
authors: Ran El-Yaniv; Yair Wiener
access_depth: Abstract and bibliographic metadata inspected; no full-text claim
contribution: Formalizes the risk–coverage trade-off for classification with a reject option.
key_findings: Characterizes achievable trade-offs and develops algorithms for noise-free settings.
importance: Offers a rigorous alternative to evaluating an abstaining system by error rate alone.
relevance: An agent that refuses every task or preserves every candidate could seem robust under a one-sided metric.
transferable_idea: Evaluate preservation of correct programs together with successful repair of defective programs; show risk as a function of actionable coverage.
limitations: Noise-free classification assumptions do not describe noisy security feedback. The transferred metric must specify what coverage means at task, candidate, and decision levels.

title: Selective Classification for Deep Neural Networks
authors: Yonatan Geifman; Ran El-Yaniv
access_depth: Abstract and bibliographic metadata inspected; no full-text claim
contribution: Constructs selective classifiers that target a desired prediction risk by rejecting uncertain examples.
key_findings: Demonstrates useful risk–coverage operating points on image-classification datasets under the method's assumptions.
importance: Shows that a method should expose controllable risk and coverage rather than just report a lower error count.
relevance: The proposed repair policy needs a way to trade audit expense, unnecessary refusal, and harmful edits.
transferable_idea: Predeclare operating points and compare methods at matched coverage or matched cost, rather than tuning each on the final evaluation set.
limitations: Its statistical guarantee applies to the specified classification/calibration setup; it cannot be asserted for a small selected security-repair cohort.

title: On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks
authors: Chuan Guo; Geoff Pleiss; Yu Sun; Kilian Q. Weinberger
access_depth: Abstract and bibliographic metadata inspected; no full-text claim
contribution: Studies whether neural-network confidence corresponds to empirical correctness.
key_findings: Modern networks can be miscalibrated; temperature scaling is effective on many evaluated datasets.
importance: Separates predictive accuracy from the reliability of confidence used in decisions.
relevance: If the follow-up asks agents how likely a checker is wrong, raw confidence should not be treated as a probability.
transferable_idea: Calibrate a decision score on development families and assess calibration separately for defective-code and defective-checker cases.
limitations: Temperature scaling of classifier logits is not automatically applicable to verbal LLM probabilities, and calibration on one task distribution does not ensure transfer.

title: When Is a Memory Safe Enough to Act On? Action-Conditioned Verification for Long-Lived Agents
authors: Yiqi Wang; Yifei Wang; Jiaqi Zhang; Zhangkai Wu; Yiqun Duan; Taotao Cai; Mingkai Zheng
access_depth: Full-text formulation, method, and evaluation-protocol sections inspected; results not independently reproduced
contribution: Formulates action-conditioned memory verification as a costed sequential proceed/verify/abstain problem.
key_findings: Reports cost reductions against static verification and analyzes reliability, consequence, and complementary checks.
importance: A direct novelty constraint on any generic proposal for value-of-information verification of agents.
relevance: The paper already uses candidate-fixed interventions, noisy verifiers, and an exact information-constrained reference.
transferable_idea: Differentiate the repair study through interventions on checker verdicts that trigger changes to executable code, with separate unsafe-acceptance and functional-denial consequences.
limitations: Preprint only. Its gate does not establish the proposed security-repair mechanism; its bounded premise-dependence model is not a general oracle.

title: Simple and Scalable Predictive Uncertainty Estimation using Deep Ensembles
authors: Balaji Lakshminarayanan; Alexander Pritzel; Charles Blundell
access_depth: Abstract and bibliographic metadata inspected; no full-text claim
contribution: Uses independently trained neural networks to estimate predictive uncertainty.
key_findings: Demonstrates competitive calibration and useful uncertainty behavior across classification, regression, and shifted inputs.
importance: Provides a relevant precedent for diversifying evaluators rather than assuming one confidence score is sufficient.
relevance: The proposed second opinion may share errors with the original checker or agent.
transferable_idea: Measure joint error tables and compare heterogeneous evidence sources with repeated calls to the same evaluator at matched cost.
limitations: Neural ensembles are not executable security validators; the paper does not guarantee independence or correctness of multiple model-generated judgments.

title: Can You Trust Your Model’s Uncertainty? Evaluating Predictive Uncertainty Under Dataset Shift
authors: Yaniv Ovadia; Emily Fertig; Jie Ren; Zachary Nado; D. Sculley; Sebastian Nowozin; Joshua V. Dillon; Balaji Lakshminarayanan; Jasper Snoek
access_depth: Primary-paper abstract and introduction inspected
contribution: Benchmarks uncertainty estimation when evaluation inputs differ from training inputs.
key_findings: Common post-hoc calibration methods can fail under shift; some model-marginalizing approaches perform more robustly.
importance: Shows why a calibrated checker-reliability estimate requires a specified deployment distribution.
relevance: A policy tuned on CSRF modes may be poorly calibrated for key rotation, arbitrary Python, or repository repair.
transferable_idea: Hold out mechanisms and change checker error distributions deliberately; test calibration, decision quality, and coverage after the shift.
limitations: The study evaluates predictive models, not code-repair agents. Its findings motivate stress tests but cannot supply numerical expectations for this project.

title: Trust in Automation: Designing for Appropriate Reliance
authors: John D. Lee; Katrina A. See
access_depth: Abstract and bibliographic metadata inspected; no full-text claim
contribution: Develops an integrated account of trust and appropriate reliance on imperfect automation.
key_findings: Reliance depends on context and automation characteristics; maximizing trust is not the appropriate design objective.
importance: A strong conceptual bridge to an AI agent relying on a security checker.
relevance: Teaching an agent to distrust FAIL indiscriminately could preserve good code while making it ignore genuine defects.
transferable_idea: Evaluate calibrated reliance across truthful and misleading PASS/FAIL, explicitly scoring both unwarranted obedience and unwarranted rejection.
limitations: This is a human-automation review, not evidence of humanlike trust in LLMs; operationalize reliance through observable decisions rather than psychological attribution.

title: Humans and Automation: Use, Misuse, Disuse, Abuse
authors: Raja Parasuraman; Victor Riley
access_depth: Abstract and bibliographic metadata inspected; no full-text claim
contribution: Distinguishes appropriate automation use from overreliance, underuse, and design-induced misuse.
key_findings: False alarms can produce disuse; reliability, workload, and system design interact in reliance decisions.
importance: Explains why both overtrust and blanket skepticism must be failure modes.
relevance: The original hidden veto and controller handshake can manufacture apparent agent failures through system design.
transferable_idea: Build symmetric controls and manipulate the history of checker reliability, while separately auditing the controller's contribution.
limitations: Human-factors categories are analytical analogies here. An agent changing code after FAIL does not by itself prove trust, complacency, or a human cognitive bias.

title: Ironies of automation
authors: Lisanne Bainbridge
access_depth: Abstract and bibliographic metadata inspected; no full-text claim
contribution: Argues that automation can leave operators with difficult abnormal situations rather than remove their burden.
key_findings: Automating routine control can expand monitoring and recovery problems at the human–machine boundary.
importance: Suggests evaluating the whole repair-and-check system instead of attributing every outcome to the model.
relevance: The draft's delayed stop handshake and hidden veto are failures of the surrounding automation that distort behavioral labels.
transferable_idea: Use scripted agents to isolate controller behavior, then compare complete systems under matched failure conditions and recovery interfaces.
limitations: The article is a conceptual analysis of industrial automation, not a benchmark of language-model agents or an estimate of their error rates.

title: The role of trust in automation reliance
authors: Mary T. Dzindolet; Scott A. Peterson; Regina A. Pomranky; Linda G. Pierce; Hall P. Beck
access_depth: Publisher abstract and study/discussion excerpts inspected
contribution: Experimentally studies reliability, trust, and reliance on an automated decision aid.
key_findings: Explaining why an aid might err increased reliance, including situations in which that trust was unwarranted.
importance: A counterintuitive warning that more explanation does not necessarily produce better calibrated decisions.
relevance: The current diagnostic-feedback condition changes wording, but explanation plausibility and evidential validity are not disentangled.
transferable_idea: Cross verdict truth with evidence validity, using plausible but invalid explanations and verifiable counterexamples; measure whether agents track evidence or persuasive form.
limitations: These are human experiments on a visual-detection task. They motivate an LLM hypothesis, not a direct prediction of the same effect.

title: Algorithm aversion: People erroneously avoid algorithms after seeing them err
authors: Berkeley J. Dietvorst; Joseph P. Simmons; Cade Massey
access_depth: Abstract and bibliographic metadata inspected; no full-text claim
contribution: Tests how observing algorithmic errors affects willingness to rely on forecasts.
key_findings: Across the studied conditions, people can reject superior algorithms after observing their mistakes.
importance: Provides a counterweight to the assumption that the only reliance problem is excessive obedience.
relevance: A training intervention warning about faulty checkers could make agents reject accurate security warnings.
transferable_idea: Include a reliability-history manipulation and measure recovery of reliance when feedback becomes accurate again.
limitations: The finding concerns human forecasting choices. Do not diagnose algorithm aversion in an LLM from a few selected repair trajectories or assume the effect is universal.

title: Algorithm appreciation: People prefer algorithmic to human judgment
authors: Jennifer M. Logg; Julia A. Minson; Don A. Moore
venue: Organizational Behavior and Human Decision Processes 151:90–103
access_depth: Abstract and bibliographic metadata inspected; no full-text claim
contribution: Shows conditions under which people give greater weight to algorithmic than human advice.
key_findings: Equivalent advice can have different influence depending on the attributed source.
importance: Challenges a universal algorithm-aversion narrative and motivates source-label controls.
relevance: A checker branded as authoritative might induce different repair behavior even when its evidence is unchanged.
transferable_idea: Randomize neutral source labels independently of verdict and evidence validity, while keeping the same executable counterexample; test whether labels dominate substance.
limitations: Human advice weighting is not an LLM mechanism. The experiment would test an analogy, and source-label effects alone would not establish irrationality.

title: Concrete Problems in AI Safety
authors: Dario Amodei; Chris Olah; Jacob Steinhardt; Paul Christiano; John Schulman; Dan Mané
access_depth: arXiv abstract and metadata inspected
contribution: Organizes practical AI safety problems around objectives, supervision cost, exploration, and distribution shift.
key_findings: Highlights how misspecified objectives and imperfect supervision can create harmful behavior without malicious intent.
importance: An influential agenda that already identifies proxy optimization and supervision failures as central problems.
relevance: The hidden veto is an imperfect supervisory signal, while weak tests are incomplete operationalizations of desired behavior.
transferable_idea: Use the taxonomy to distinguish corrupted feedback from unsafe exploration and from genuine repair inability, with separate experiments for each.
limitations: This is an agenda-setting preprint, not evidence of a measured causal effect in code repair and not a source for a security-success rate.

title: Inverse Reward Design
authors: Dylan Hadfield-Menell; Smitha Milli; Pieter Abbeel; Stuart Russell; Anca D. Dragan
access_depth: Abstract and bibliographic metadata inspected; no full-text claim
contribution: Treats a designed reward as evidence about intended objectives in the context where the reward was constructed.
key_findings: Inferring uncertainty about intended reward can reduce undesirable behavior when moving to new situations.
importance: Offers a conceptual alternative to treating checker output as an unquestionable objective.
relevance: The hidden veto and narrow tests may conflict with the user's actual security and functionality requirements.
transferable_idea: Give agents explicit task contracts and uncertainty about checker scope, then test whether they preserve those contracts when feedback conflicts.
limitations: Reward inference in modeled environments differs from interpreting a security test; the transfer must not become a license to ignore valid specifications.

title: Reinforcement Learning with a Corrupted Reward Channel
authors: Tom Everitt; Victoria Krakovna; Laurent Orseau; Marcus Hutter; Shane Legg
access_depth: Official proceedings abstract and primary-paper introduction inspected
contribution: Formalizes reinforcement learning when observed reward differs systematically from the intended reward.
key_findings: Standard reinforcement learning can perform poorly even under simplified corruption; richer evidence or limited optimization can help under assumptions.
importance: A close theoretical antecedent for separating true properties from delivered feedback.
relevance: The veto changes the feedback channel independently of code quality, though the evaluated agent is not trained online by RL.
transferable_idea: Represent checker corruption separately from program state and measure when an extra information source can identify the faulty channel.
limitations: Exogenous corruption is not necessarily deliberate reward hacking. The PDF footnote credits Hutter as fourth author despite his omission from the proceedings listing.

title: Defining and Characterizing Reward Gaming
authors: Joar Skalse; Nikolaus H. R. Howe; Dmitrii Krasheninnikov; David Krueger
access_depth: Official abstract and primary-paper abstract/introduction inspected
contribution: Formalizes conditions under which optimizing a proxy reward can worsen a true reward.
key_findings: Unhackability is highly restrictive across broad policy classes; restricted policy sets permit different relationships.
importance: Prevents treating proxy alignment as obvious merely because a benchmark works on a few examples.
relevance: The finite-mode suites restrict policy classes, while real Python repair admits many more ways to satisfy shallow checks.
transferable_idea: Test whether apparent feedback robustness survives expansion from fixed modes to richer executable programs, with independently validated outcomes.
limitations: The official landing title says Reward Gaming; the linked manuscript says Reward Hacking. Neither theorem directly characterizes LLM repair trajectories.

title: Scaling Laws for Reward Model Overoptimization
authors: Leo Gao; John Schulman; Jacob Hilton
access_depth: Abstract and bibliographic metadata inspected; no full-text claim
contribution: Measures how optimization against an imperfect learned reward can reduce performance under a separate gold-standard reward model.
key_findings: Different optimization procedures exhibit different relationships between optimization strength and gold-model score.
importance: Suggests that more search or more model capability need not monotonically improve the underlying objective.
relevance: The repair loop optimizes against finite feedback, so increased edit budget could amplify evaluator weaknesses.
transferable_idea: Vary optimization budget and checker quality jointly, measuring the full trajectory of security and functionality rather than terminal acceptance alone.
limitations: The gold reward is itself a synthetic model proxy; these scaling relationships are not expected numerical laws for security repair.

title: Constrained Policy Optimization
authors: Joshua Achiam; David Held; Aviv Tamar; Pieter Abbeel
access_depth: Abstract and bibliographic metadata inspected; no full-text claim
contribution: Optimizes reinforcement-learning policies with explicit constraints alongside reward.
key_findings: Provides near-constraint-satisfaction guarantees under the analysis and demonstrates constrained control on simulated locomotion tasks.
importance: Illustrates why security constraints should not disappear inside a single scalar task score.
relevance: The current oracle-insecure label merges harmful acceptance and unnecessary denial, which can move in opposite directions.
transferable_idea: Specify security constraints and a separate usefulness objective; report both and state any utility weights instead of choosing them after results.
limitations: The algorithm and its guarantees do not transfer directly to black-box code editing; use the constrained formulation as a design principle.

title: A Comprehensive Survey on Safe Reinforcement Learning
authors: Javier García; Fernando Fernández
access_depth: Abstract and bibliographic metadata inspected; no full-text claim
contribution: Organizes safe reinforcement-learning approaches by changes to the objective and changes to exploration.
key_findings: Separates safety during learning from safety during later deployment, including external guidance and risk-sensitive criteria.
importance: Useful for distinguishing exploratory unsafe candidates from the final deployed artifact.
relevance: The manuscript already observes temporary failures whose direction differs from terminal regression counts.
transferable_idea: Report any-time unsafe behavior, duration until recovery, and terminal correctness as distinct outcomes; decide whether attempted code is executed or only evaluated.
limitations: This survey supplies a taxonomy rather than new causal evidence. Its safety definitions are domain-dependent and should not be imported without an explicit threat model.

title: Safe Reinforcement Learning via Shielding
authors: Mohammed Alshiekh; Roderick Bloem; Rüdiger Ehlers; Bettina Könighofer; Scott Niekum; Ufuk Topcu
access_depth: Abstract and bibliographic metadata inspected; no full-text claim
contribution: Synthesizes a reactive shield that modifies proposed actions when necessary to enforce temporal-logic requirements.
key_findings: Demonstrates a way to combine learning with specification-based protection under explicit model assumptions.
importance: Provides a meaningful stronger baseline than merely asking an agent to be cautious.
relevance: The paper's paired continuations could compare optional advice with an enforcement mechanism that preserves validated properties.
transferable_idea: Keep an independently validated candidate and prevent replacement unless security and functionality checks pass; measure when this conservative baseline blocks useful repairs.
limitations: A shield inherits specification errors and model limitations. The contribution cannot be simply claiming that an external guard is new or guarantees general code security.
